newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major set to balk on EMU first wave -- paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major set to balk on EMU first wave -- paper.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major will in the next few months give the clearest possible signal that Britain will not join a single currency in the first wave if his ruling Conservatives win the next general election, the Financial Times (FT) newspaper said on Tuesday.

Major, who has a one-seat majority in parliament, is unlikely to formally rule out British participation in the first wave, for fear of prompting a damaging resignation by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, the FT said.
"The gains of having a firmer policy against monetary union would be offset by the inevitable row with the chancellor," the FT quoted an unnamed "close colleague" of Major.
"Anyway, everyone knows we would not go in if elected for a fifth term."
British finance minister Clarke on Monday dismissed as preposterous a report that his government was about to ditch its wait-and-see stance on a single European Union currency.

At a meeting of EU finance ministers in Brussels, Clarke said that opting out of a single currency now would be "no way to fight an election nor present yourself to the country as a governing party at all".

The comments, made to BBC radio, were widely viewed in Brussels as the closest the pro-European Chancellor of the Exchequer has come to threatening to resign if his Conservative Party shifts its policy in a more "Euro-sceptic" direction.
